change.title: pr-4
change.description: FEATURE: Embeddable Discourse comments, now with simple-rss instead of feedzirra
change.author: Robin Ward

findings.title: raw_html posts store and serve remote HTML with no sanitization (stored XSS on the forum origin)
findings.body: `cook` returns `raw` untouched for `raw_html` posts. That skips PrettyText and its sanitizer. `PostCreator.before_create_tasks` (lib/post_creator.rb:105) and `Post`'s `before_save` (post.rb:321) both store whatever `cook` returns as `cooked`. `ProcessPost` does the same at app/jobs/regular/process_post.rb:13. The remote HTML comes from two places. One is a feed item, via `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)` in poll_feed.rb:35, which has no tag filtering. The other is `Readability` in `import_remote`. That one allows `href`/`src`, so `javascript:` URLs pass. `TopicEmbed.import` also interpolates `url` into `<a href='#{url}'>` without escaping (topic_embed.rb:13). The only check on `url` is `=~ /^https?:\/\//`, which has no `$` and uses a line-start `^`, so a `'` in the URL breaks out of the attribute. The result is rendered raw in the embed iframe (`raw post.cooked`, best.html.erb:19) and as normal post HTML on the main site. A `<script>` or `javascript:` link in a feed item or fetched page therefore runs on the forum origin for every viewer, admins included. Fix: sanitize the imported HTML before storing it, for example with Sanitize/Loofah and a tag and attribute whitelist that rejects `javascript:`. Escape `url` in the footer with `ERB::Util.h`.

findings.title: embed.css and embed.js are not in the precompile list, so the feature breaks in production
findings.body: `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` needs `embed.css`, and the snippet in the PR needs `embed.js`. Neither is added to `config.assets.precompile` (config/application.rb:61 lists only vendor.js, common.css, desktop.css and the others). config/environments/production.rb:23 sets `assets.compile = false`. In production the layout therefore raises, or links to a stylesheet that was never built, and `embed.js` cannot be served. Tests pass because test.rb:40 sets `assets.compile = true`. Add `'embed.js', 'embed.css'` to the precompile list. config/application.rb is not part of this PR.

findings.title: Anyone who forges a Referer can enqueue fetches, and so create topics, for arbitrary URLs on the embeddable host
findings.body: `ensure_embeddable` trusts the client-supplied Referer (line 26). Any script can send `Referer: http://<embeddable_host>/`, and the host is public. The `embed_url` is never checked in the controller. Line 15 enqueues `retrieve_topic` for any value. The job checks the host only against `embed_url` (topic_retriever.rb:15). The throttle is per URL (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`, topic_retriever.rb:26), and the anon cache is keyed by `REQUEST_URI`. Requesting `embed/best?embed_url=http://host/x?1`, then `?2`, and so on gives an unauthenticated caller as many jobs as they like. Each job that gets a 200 page (any site that ignores query strings) creates a new topic, post and `TopicEmbed` under `embed_by_username`. That is topic spam and unbounded outbound fetching. Validate in the controller that the `embed_url` host equals `embeddable_host`. Consider also normalizing the URL (dropping the query and fragment) before using it as the key, and rate limiting job creation per IP.

findings.title: The anon cache serves the page without running the referer check
findings.body: `discourse_expires_in` stores the full response, including the `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` header, in Redis under `HTTP_HOST + REQUEST_URI` for 1 minute (lib/middleware/anonymous_cache.rb:14, 49-60). `AnonymousCache#call` returns a hit before the app runs (anonymous_cache.rb:83), so for 60 seconds after one valid request `ensure_embeddable` is skipped. Any referer, or none, gets the framable page. The page is public content, but the `embeddable_host` restriction does not hold during that window. The cached HTML also bakes in the first requester's `request.referer` (see the layout finding). A cache hit also skips the `Jobs.enqueue` on line 15.

findings.title: postMessage targetOrigin is the full Referer, but the response is cached per URL, not per referer
findings.body: The cached response (anonymous_cache.rb:14) is reused for other embedders. `ensure_embeddable` compares only the host, so `http://site.com/a` and `https://site.com/b` both pass. If the cached page was rendered for one origin and is shown in a parent with another (http vs https, or a different port), `postMessage` silently drops the `discourse-resize` message. The iframe then stays at its default height with `scrolling=no`, so the comments are clipped. A Referer ending in a backslash also breaks the JS string. Compute only the origin (scheme://host[:port]) and `j`/`to_json`-escape it. Alternatively, use `'*'`, since the message carries only a height.

findings.title: The loading page reloads forever, and retrieval failures are silent
findings.body: Nothing bounds the wait. The page reloads every 30s indefinitely (lines 8-10). Each reload on a cache miss enqueues `retrieve_topic` again, because `best` enqueues whenever no `TopicEmbed` exists. If retrieval can never succeed, the visitor sees 'Loading Discussion...' for as long as the page is open. Possible causes are the page returning 404 (`open(url).read` raises in the job), no `embed_by_username` user (`fetch_http` returns silently, topic_retriever.rb:50), or the URL being throttled or on the wrong host. The job runs, fails or returns, and the viewer is never told. Consider a retry cap (a counter in the URL or in `sessionStorage`) followed by a failure message, and logging the reason when the retriever returns early.

findings.title: Origin check is a substring match
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` passes whenever `e.origin` is any substring of `discourseUrl`. That includes an empty string, `http://a` for `http://abc.com/`, and a bare `http://forum`. Any window that can message the host page can then set the iframe height. The impact is limited to layout. Compare exact origins instead, for example by parsing `discourseUrl` into an anchor element and comparing `protocol//host`. Line 5 also throws if `#discourse-comments` is missing.

findings.title: A failed PostCreator.create is treated as success
findings.body: `PostCreator#create` returns `@post` even after `save_post` raises `ActiveRecord::Rollback` (lib/post_creator.rb:231-236, 86). It also returns an unsaved post when `rollback_if_host_spam_detected` fires. `post.present?` is therefore true for an unsaved post. `TopicEmbed.create!` then runs with `post_id: nil` and fails on the NOT NULL column, not with the creator's `errors`. Because of the nested `Topic.transaction`, the inner Rollback is swallowed. Check `post.persisted?` or `creator.errors` and skip the embed instead. `import` also appends to the caller's `contents` string (line 13), which mutates the argument.

findings.title: One bad feed item aborts the whole poll
findings.body: The loop has no per-item rescue. An item with no `content` (RSS items that only have `description`) raises NoMethodError on `i.content.scrub`. A `TopicEmbed.import` error, such as the unique index on `embed_url` racing with `RetrieveTopic`, also raises. Either one ends `execute`. `sidekiq_options retry: false` means the remaining items wait an hour, and the same item fails again each time. `i.link`/`i.id` can also be nil. Rescue and log per item, and fall back to `i.description` when `content` is blank. Line 29 uses `Kernel#open` on an admin-set string (a value starting with `|` runs a command), where `URI.parse(url).open` would not.

findings.title: SETNX followed by EXPIRE is not atomic
findings.body: If the process dies between `setnx` and `expire`, the key never expires. That URL can never be retrieved by non-staff again, and nothing tells anyone why. Use a single `$redis.set(key, 1, nx: true, ex: 60)` if the redis gem version supports it. Otherwise use `setex` guarded by an `exists` check.

findings.title: `force: true` added to an existing migration and to the new create_topic_embeds
findings.body: `create_table ... force: true` runs `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` first. If either migration is run again, for example after a manual rollback of the schema_migrations row or on a partially migrated DB, it silently drops `top_topics` or `topic_embeds` and their data. Editing a migration that has already shipped (create_top_topics) is unrelated to this feature, and the PR does not say why it is needed. The same applies to db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3. The whitespace-only edit to 20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb is noise. Drop the `force: true` options and the unrelated edits unless there is a stated reason.

findings.title: Adding a NOT NULL column with a default to the posts table rewrites it
findings.body: On PostgreSQL 9.x (the README minimum is 9.1+), `add_column :posts, ..., default: 1, null: false` rewrites the whole table under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock. On a large forum that blocks reads and writes of posts for the duration. Adding the column nullable, then setting the default, then backfilling in batches avoids the rewrite. The default 1 matches `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`, so the values themselves are right.

findings.title: `<%- end if %>` is a modifier `if` whose condition is the next output statement
findings.body: This is not valid as a plain `end`. It works only because Erubis emits the following `@output_buffer.safe_concat` as the modifier's condition, and that value happens to be truthy. Use `<%- end %>`.

findings.title: Disqus import drops --category and now does a live HTTP fetch per thread
findings.body: The `--category` option (removed at line 116 and in the old lines 142-146) is deleted without being mentioned in the PR, so existing invocations lose their category without any error. The importer now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`. That fetches every thread URL over HTTP, with no host check and no rescue. One 404 or timeout, or a nil `t[:link]`, aborts the whole import part-way. It also stores the remote page as a `raw_html` post instead of a permalink stub, so it carries the sanitization issue above. If this is intended, restore the category option and rescue per thread.

findings.title: Specs pass for the wrong reason, and key paths are untested
findings.body: 'is 404 without an embed_url' never reaches the param check. `embeddable_host` is blank, so `ensure_embeddable` raises InvalidAccess first. `response.should_not be_success` also passes for any 403/500. The two success specs run the job inline only because `queue_jobs?` is false in test (app/jobs/base.rb:162-173). Despite its name, the 'tells the topic retriever' spec exercises `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` through `TopicRetriever.new`. Nothing tests the `retrieve_topic` job, `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` or `fetch_http`, a revise that keeps `cook_method` raw_html, `TopicEmbed.import` updating an existing embed (the 'Supports updating the post' spec at spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:39 does not check the sha1 or revision), or the rejected-host path (`topic_retriever_spec` stubs `perform_retrieve`). Assert on status codes (403/400) and add specs for these paths.

contracts.action: The embed page enqueues a background retrieval and shows a loading page that reloads itself
contracts.equivalent_path: Other controllers' anonymous caching via `discourse_expires_in`; `Jobs.enqueue` in app/jobs/base.rb:153-175
contracts.before_after: Before: no such path. After: if no TopicEmbed exists, `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic)` is called and 'loading' is rendered, which reloads every 30s (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:8-10). The job runs `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, which skips on an invalid host or a throttled URL (lib/topic_retriever.rb:9). Otherwise it runs PollFeed (when enabled) and then an HTTP fetch via `TopicEmbed.import_remote`.
contracts.visible_effect: The iframe shows 'Loading Discussion...' until a TopicEmbed row exists, then the next reload (30s) or cache expiry shows the best posts.
contracts.failure_mode: Nothing bounds the wait. The reload loop has no cap. Job failures (404, open-uri error), a missing `embed_by_username` user (topic_retriever.rb:50) and throttling or an invalid host all end silently, and the visitor sees 'Loading...' forever. The job has no timeout or rescue of its own. With `queue_jobs?` false the fetch blocks the web request (base.rb:168-173).

contracts.action: The embed response is cached in the anonymous cache for 1 minute
contracts.before_after: The cache key is host plus REQUEST_URI (anonymous_cache.rb:14). A hit short-circuits before the controller (anonymous_cache.rb:83), so `ensure_embeddable`, the job enqueue and the per-request `request.referer` in the layout are all skipped or frozen to the first requester.
contracts.visible_effect: Within 60s, requests with a different or missing referer get the framable page. Embedders on a different origin get a page whose postMessage targetOrigin does not match theirs, so the height is never applied.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent: the resize message is dropped and the iframe is clipped. The referer restriction is bypassed.

contracts.action: Posts created via PostCreator with cook_method raw_html skip the cooking pipeline
contracts.equivalent_path: Regular posts: `post_analyzer.cook` via PrettyText with the `after_post_cook` filter (post.rb:136); re-cooking in the before_save (post.rb:321) and in ProcessPost (process_post.rb:13)
contracts.before_after: The new path returns `raw` unchanged from every cook call site: PostCreator.before_create_tasks (post_creator.rb:105), the Post before_save on revision, and ProcessPost. Sanitization and the plugin filter are skipped, and `cooking_options` are ignored.
contracts.visible_effect: Imported HTML appears verbatim on the main site and in the embed iframe.
contracts.failure_mode: Remote script or `javascript:` content is stored and executed on the forum origin. See the XSS finding.

contracts.action: TopicEmbed.import creates a post through PostCreator inside Topic.transaction and then a TopicEmbed row
contracts.equivalent_path: PostCreator.create callers (e.g. posts_controller) that check `creator.errors` before using the result
contracts.before_after: The new caller checks only `post.present?`, but PostCreator returns `@post` even after a Rollback (post_creator.rb:86, 231-236).
contracts.visible_effect: On creator failure the import raises a NOT NULL violation from `create!` instead of returning nil. In RetrieveTopic or PollFeed that surfaces as a failed job, and in the Disqus task as an aborted import.
contracts.failure_mode: The error is raised, not silent, but the message is misleading and PollFeed stops processing later items.

contracts.action: embed.js posts a message listener and receives height messages from the iframe
contracts.before_after: The listener accepts any message whose `e.origin` is a substring of `discourseUrl` and sets the iframe height. The listener is never removed.
contracts.visible_effect: The iframe is resized on the embedding page.
contracts.failure_mode: A message from an origin that is a substring of the discourse URL is accepted. If the iframe never sends a message (see the cache and referer finding), the height stays at the default and the content is clipped, with no error.

summary: The embed feature has one serious problem and several smaller ones. Imported `raw_html` posts skip all HTML sanitization (`app/models/post.rb:133`), which is a stored-XSS risk on the forum origin. `embed.js` and `embed.css` are not in `config.assets.precompile`, and production runs with `assets.compile = false`, so the embed page will not work there. The Referer-only access check is spoofable, and combined with per-URL throttling it lets anyone trigger fetches and topic creation. The 1-minute anon cache skips the referer check on a hit and bakes the first requester's referer into the postMessage origin. The loading page reloads forever with no failure state. Smaller issues: `TopicEmbed.import` treats an unsaved post as success, one bad feed item aborts the whole poll, the Disqus task silently loses `--category`, and the specs pass for the wrong reason or leave key paths untested. I read the PR's source, view, migration and spec files plus the callers they touch. Nothing was built or run, so none of this was run to confirm it.
